messages:
Rina (CS): creating a short "Launchpad" handout for new customers (prefill, batching, streaming). Goal: tiny doc they can paste into their runbook and support tickets. Can I get quick sanity checks?
Omar (SRE): looks good. Add a 'dry-run' step: issue a prefill with low tokens and verify prefix_cache_hit_rate climbs above 50% within 15m.
Jules (Solutions): Agree. Also recommend a short warm-pool (1 GPU for 24h) for mid-size customers. Cost note included.
Evan (CS Ops): For renewal-watchlist accounts, propose 10-day active probe: days 0-4 daily, days 5-9 every other day. Capture metrics: prefix_cache_hit_rate, stream_error_rate, p95_latency, token_delta, model_fallback_count.
Rina (CS): adding those. Draft pasteable ticket checklist: 1) prefill run & verification 2) warm-pool requested 3) batching params set 4) streaming fallback enabled 5) telemetry probes attached 6) cost cap tag applied.
Omar (SRE): small config example for customers:
```
serving:
  prefill:
    tokens: 300
    ttl_seconds: 7200
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 12
    adaptive: true
    jitter_ms: 40-180
  streaming:
    fallback_to_sync: true
    max_chunk_delay_ms: 90
monitoring:
  probes: [prefix_cache_hit_rate, stream_error_rate, latency_p95, token_delta]
```
Jules (Solutions): and a one-liner for the UI team: "Debounce token render to 120ms to avoid flicker when switching between cached and live tokens."
Evan (CS Ops): small shell snippet to pull probes for tickets:
```
# fetch probes for tenant
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://metrics.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/kestrelco/probes?from=-24h" | jq .
```
redwood-alert-bot: scheduled infra maintenance 2025-06-12 03:00 UTC — warm-pool spinups may be rate-limited.
Rina (CS): thanks all. I'll finalize the one-pager, include a 2-row CSV template (date, prefix_cache_hit_rate, stream_error_rate, p95_latency, token_delta, notes) and push to onboarding. Tagging @Jules for final config approval. :thumbsup:
